subject: Follow-up: SummitAI evaluation — candidate models, prompt set & quant tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@summitai.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@summitai.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: SummitAI evaluation — candidate models, prompt set & quant tradeoffs

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard (short):
- Primary goal: replace current cloud LLM for customer support triage and first-pass summarization while reducing per-token cost by ~3x.
- SLO targets: 95th pct token-latency ~<150ms for interactive routing; throughput target for batch re-runs ~800 reqs/min.
- Data: internal transcripts + support KB (we’ll get a 3k-prompt eval slice from you).

Suggested candidate models for the evaluation run (we picked models to span quality/throughput):
- Llama-2-13B-chat — strong conversational baseline; good community tooling for GPTQ/AWQ quantizations.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct — high throughput per GPU, smaller memory footprint for caching.
- OpenAssistant-13B (instruction tuned) — higher quality on instruction-following use cases.

Quant/options we recommend testing in parallel:
- AWQ (4-bit) — biggest cost reduction on many LLMs, but can increase generation variance on long-form prompts.
- GPTQ (4-bit/8-bit) — often preserves quality better than naive 4-bit but has more conversion friction and kernel dependency.
- FP8 (dynamic) — near-floating-point quality with smaller memory footprint; higher runtime cost than 4-bit options.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) You drop the eval prompt set (3k items) into the attached summitai_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (or share a Drive link) — we already have a placeholder.
2) Redwood runs a lightweight trade study across the three candidate models + quant settings (AWQ-4, GPTQ-4, GPTQ-8, FP8) and returns per-model: latency (p50/p95 per-token), tokens/sec, avg score on your evaluation rubric, and rough cost-per-1M-tokens.
3) We’ll flag any quality regressions by prompt category (summarization, triage, escalation) and recommend a canary configuration for a small production test.

Attachments included: summitai_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (placeholder), summitai_quant_trade_study_v1.pdf (high-level trade study template).

Timeline proposal: 48–72 hours for initial trade study (engineering dependent).

If that sounds good I’ll schedule the run and loop in engineering (cc’d Serg and Vivek).

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim | Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

- Eval slice: we’ll export the 3k prompts by EOD today (will ping Priya).

If you can include the retention/access answers in the run notes that would be great. Looking forward to the trade study.

Thanks — quick plan and preliminary notes: 

Plan
- Kick off parallel conversions for Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B to AWQ-4 and GPTQ-4 (and a GPTQ-8 baseline). FP8 runs will use the FP8-enabled runtime path.
- Run the 3k-prompt set in batched mode (50 per batch) for throughput numbers and run a smaller interactive simulation for p95 token latency.
- Produce a single CSV with per-model/per-quant rows: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, avg rubric score, hallucination-rate.

Prelim findings (sanity check; full numbers attached in summitai_quant_prelim_results.csv):
- AWQ-4 (Llama-2-13B): ~2.8x memory reduction vs fp16, p95 token-latency improved ~2.1x in our runtime, but we saw a +4–6% drop on the rubric for long-form summarization prompts compared to GPTQ-8.
- GPTQ-4: quality closer to fp16 (approx +1–2% rubric delta) but conversion time is longer and runtime kernels are less mature on some GPU stacks; throughput is slightly lower than AWQ on small-batch interactive tests.
- FP8: preserves near-fp16 quality, latency is worse vs AWQ but better than unoptimized fp16 in some setups; cost is higher than 4-bit options.

Retention / logs
- By default eval artifacts (logs, raw outputs) live in a customer-scoped S3 bucket for 30 days and are accessible only to the customer + Redwood engineering. We can shorten retention to 7 days or provide an air-gapped export on request. Suggest documenting this in the handoff note to SummitAI.

Next steps
- I’ll upload the preliminary CSV (summitai_quant_prelim_results.csv) + run config (eval-config.yaml) to the console link and follow up with a cleaned per-model cost table (tokens/second -> est $/1M tokens) tomorrow.
- If SummitAI wants to prioritize quality for summarization, recommend starting with GPTQ-8 on Llama-2-13B for the canary; if cost is paramount, AWQ-4 on Mistral-7B is the best cost/throughput trade.

ETA for full report: +24 hours. Blockers: need the final 3k prompt file and confirmation on whether we can preserve placeholders for PII or must redact.

-Vivek
